plain_claim: Assume that a destructor panic during unwinding aborts the process and let s be a forward (acyclic, topologically numbered) toy program that only mentions valid move paths, moves only definitely-initialized places (call arguments pairwise disjoint), initializes only definitely-uninitialized places, and has no resume node reachable from the entry along normal edges only. Then the standard decision map is elaboration-correct, and every elaboration-correct decision map (same CFG, one flag per atom, standard flag maintenance) tests every atom that the standard map tests at some forward-reachable drop point; so the standard flag set is the least flag set among elaboration-correct decision maps of this class.

hypotheses.name: hfwd : Forward s
hypotheses.purpose: the one-pass initialization analyses follow index-increasing edges only, which are all edges exactly when the program is forward (acyclic, topologically numbered)
hypotheses.witness_class: a 1-local (leaf), 3-node program with one back edge (progLoop)

hypotheses.name: hplaces : PlacesAreMovePaths s
hypotheses.purpose: every mentioned place follows its local's type and never enters a struct with its own destructor, so the analysis's atoms match the units written and destroyed
hypotheses.witness_class: a 1-local, 3-node forward program whose local is a struct with its own destructor and two leaf fields (progDropStruct)

hypotheses.name: hmoves : MovesFromInit s
hypotheses.purpose: no use after move: every moved place (and call argument) is must-init, and call arguments are pairwise disjoint
hypotheses.witness_class: a 1-local (leaf), 4-node forward program (progUseAfterMove)

hypotheses.name: hinits : InitsIntoUninit s
hypotheses.purpose: no overwrite of an owned value: every initialized place (and call destination not overlapped by an argument) is not may-init
hypotheses.witness_class: a 1-local (leaf), 3-node forward program (progOverwrite)

hypotheses.name: hclean : NoNormalPathToResume s
hypotheses.purpose: no resume node is reachable from the entry along normal edges only, so a resume ladder (whose drops have no landing pad) runs only while unwinding, where a destructor panic aborts
hypotheses.witness_class: a 2-local (two leaves), 3-node forward program (progResumeNormal)

non_claims: The class of elaborations compared is fixed: the source CFG is kept, there is one flag per atom (maintained at every init, move and call), and only the per-(drop point, atom) decision varies. Elaborations outside this class can use fewer flags: duplicating the join (dupProg_matches_stdElab_progJoin), sharing one flag across atoms whose states are correlated (shareProg_matches_stdElab_progShare), and dropping early on one branch before a shared exit (earlyDropProg_matches_stdElab_progJoin), all proved for one program each; encoding initialization in memory by zeroing or value niches is not modelled; correlated branch predicates can make one side of a may-init-but-not-must-init split infeasible (not proved here).

`Ty.atoms` splits every struct without its own destructor eagerly into its fields, like RFC 320's structural drop obligations. rustc creates child move paths only for projections that occur in the body and drops the remaining fields under the parent's flag, so for a struct moved only as a whole it uses one flag where flagSet of the standard map counts two (derived (modeling bridge); not proved here).

Branches, call panics and destructor panics are independent free input bits; the theorem quantifies over all of them, not over the feasible paths of a real program. With correlated conditions a flag the analysis requires can be semantically unnecessary (not proved here).

The results concern acyclic (forward) programs; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims for programs with loops, whose fixpoint analyses are not modelled (stdElab_fails_without_forward shows that the one-pass analysis is wrong on a loop).

These are statements about the toy model; they neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about rustc, LLVM, a C++ implementation or any real program (model–system relation: none proved). Connections to real systems are separate derived (modeling bridge) claims.
